questions.question: A four-year term insurance pays a death benefit only when death occurs before year 4. The insured survives for six years. What payment does this contract make?
options: No benefit payment.
A benefit at year 4 because the term has ended.
A benefit at year 6 when the insured eventually dies.
Return all premiums at year 4 because no claim occurred.

questions.question: A five-year term insurance covers deaths in the interval [0,5) and settles covered deaths at the end of their death year. The insured dies at time 4.7 years. Which settlement follows?
options: No benefit is paid because the settlement date reaches expiry.
The benefit is paid at time 4.7.
The benefit is paid at time 5.
The benefit is paid at time 4.

questions.question: A unit term benefit pays immediately if $T<n$. Assume $T>0$ almost surely, $0<v<1$ and $0<p=P(T<n)<1$, where $v$ is the annual discount factor. An actuary quotes its APV as $p$. Which correction is guaranteed?
options: The APV equals $p$, because each covered benefit is one.
The APV is positive and strictly below $p$.
The APV exceeds $p$, because death time is random.
The APV is zero, because some lives survive expiry.

questions.question: A unit two-year term settles at death-year end with zero interest. First-year death probability is $q=0.2$; conditional on surviving that year, next-year death probability is also $q$. A student quotes APV $2q$. Which missing step explains the error?
options: Square each annual rate, because two years are covered.
Subtract overlap, because the two death-year events overlap.
Set APV to one, because zero interest makes payment certain.
Weight the second conditional rate by first-year survival.

questions.question: A unit n-year term insurance pays at death only when future lifetime $T<n$. Interest is zero, so $v=1$, and $P(T<n)$ lies strictly between zero and one. Which expression gives its APV for every such covered-death probability?
options: $P(T\geq n)$

questions.question: A unit three-year term insurance pays immediately at death if $T<3$. Annual discount factor is $v=0.9$ and realised future lifetime is $T=2.3$ years. What is the realised PV?

A unit two-year term insurance settles at death-year end. Annual discount factor is $v=0.8$, first-year death probability is $q_x=0.1$, and second-year death probability conditional on first-year survival is $q_{x+1}=0.2$. What is its APV?

A unit ten-year term insurance pays immediately at death. Its constant mortality force is $\lambda=0.02$ per year and constant interest force is $\delta=0.03$ per year, so lifetime density is $\lambda \mathrm{e}^{-\lambda t}$ and financial discount is $\mathrm{e}^{-\delta t}$. What is its APV?
A unit term death benefit has APV 0.1 on a specified coverage, settlement and mortality basis. The benefit is changed to 500 on the same basis. What is its APV?
A term death benefit has unconditional APV 0.3. Its covered-death event has probability 0.5 and PV is zero outside that event. What is mean PV conditional on a covered death?

Let $Z_n=Bv^T\mathbf1_{\{T<n\}}$ be PV of an immediate term benefit $B>0$, with future lifetime $T\geq0$ and annual discount factor $v>0$. For $n_2>n_1>0$, assume both APVs are finite. What is the necessary and sufficient condition for $E[Z_{n_2}]>E[Z_{n_1}]$?
options: $P(T\geq n_2)>0$

questions.question: A fixed positive unit term benefit covers deaths $T<n$ and is compared under immediate payment and payment at year end $\lfloor T\rfloor+1$. The annual discount factor satisfies $0<v\leq1$. Which relation between their finite APVs is guaranteed?
options: Immediate APV is strictly larger on every mortality basis.
Annual-settlement APV is at least the immediate APV.
The APVs agree whenever the coverage term is an integer.
Immediate APV is at least the annual-settlement APV.

questions.question: For a continuous future lifetime $T$ that is finite with probability one and annual discount factor $v>0$, let $A_n=E[v^T\mathbf1_{\{T<n\}}]$ be immediate term APV. Suppose matching whole-life APV $A=E[v^T]$ is finite. What is the limit as $n$ increases without bound?
options: $A_n$ approaches 1 because eventual death is certain.
$A_n$ increases weakly to $A$.
$A_n$ decreases to $A$ because distant deaths are less valuable.
$A_n$ approaches zero because its cutoff moves to infinity.

questions.question: Future lifetime $T$ is uniform on $(0,4)$ years, with density $f(t)=1/4$ there and zero elsewhere. A unit two-year term benefit pays immediately when $T<2$. Interest force is $\delta=\ln2$ per year, so the time-t discount is $2^{-t}$. What is its APV?

A unit annual-settlement term is extended from two to three years. The annual discount factor is $v=0.9$, survival to year 2 is $ {}_2p_x=0.7$, and next-year death probability conditional on that survival is $q_{x+2}=0.1$. By how much does APV increase?

A unit five-year immediate term benefit has zero interest and APV 0.2. The lifetime law has constant mortality force $\lambda>0$, so $P(T>t)=\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda t}$. Which mortality force fits this quote?

A unit n-year term benefit pays immediately at death. Let $n>0$, constant mortality force $\lambda>0$, density $f(t)=\lambda \mathrm{e}^{-\lambda t}$ and financial discount $\mathrm{e}^{-\delta t}$. For this question allow negative interest and set $\delta=-\lambda$. The usual quotient $\lambda[1-\mathrm{e}^{-(\lambda+\delta)n}]/(\lambda+\delta)$ is unavailable. What is the actual APV?
options: $\lambda n$
$0$ because its quotient numerator is zero.
$1-\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda n}$ because mortality still bounds payment probability.
$\lambda n \mathrm{e}^{\lambda n}$ because all payments must be grown to maturity.

questions.question: Two unit immediate term benefits share the same coverage length. On basis A, covered-death probability is 0.2 and conditional mean of the death-time discount factor on covered death is 0.9. On basis B, these quantities are 0.5 and 0.1 respectively. Can covered-death probability alone justify saying that B has the larger APV?
options: Yes: B has the larger APV because 0.5 exceeds 0.2.
No: A has APV 0.18 and B has APV 0.05.
No: both APVs must agree because the coverage length agrees.
Yes: B has APV 0.45 and A has APV 0.02.

questions.question: On annual discount factor 0.8, proposed unit annual-settlement term APVs for the same life are 0.08 for one-year coverage and 0.70 for two-year coverage. Which assessment correctly tests consistency of these quotes?
options: They are consistent because both prices lie between 0 and 1.
They are consistent because the two-year price exceeds the one-year price.
They are inconsistent because a two-year term price must equal the square of its one-year price.
They are inconsistent: the implied second-year conditional death rate exceeds 1.

questions.question: At issue, future lifetime $T$ is uniform on $(0,4)$ years. A unit three-year term pays immediately at death when $T<3$, and annual discount factor is $v=0.8$. The life has now survived two years. Valued at the current time 2, what is the conditional APV of its remaining covered benefit?
